stances.claim: The CA correctly reversed the OMB on two grounds: (a) CSC has primary jurisdiction over civil-service personnel actions like the 285 MIAA reassignments, so the OMB's decision was premature without a prior CSC ruling; and (b) the OMB's verdict 'lack[ed] factual basis and substantial support in evidence,' offering only 'a general statement' without adequate factual bases.
stances.confidence: asserted with the CA decision's own bolded language

stances.claim: The OMB's plenary power as 'protector of the people' under Article XI Section 5 should be exercised 'with the diligent observance of the constitutional rights of the respondents, and the constitutional powers and duties of the other agencies of the government, like the CSC, an independent coequal of the OMB.'
stances.rhetorical_move: coequality-of-independent-bodies framing (OMB is plenary but not supreme over CSC)

stances.claim: Justice Conchita Carpio Morales is 'perhaps the most celebrated OMB' -- relentlessly filing cases against the highest incumbent and retired officials including those who appointed her, regardless of political consequence.
stances.confidence: asserted with documentary recognition (Filipino of the Year, UP honoris causa, Magsaysay Award)

stances.claim: Carpio Morales is 'a hero to many and a heel to others' -- admirers cite her courage; critics fault her for 'baseless' charges leading to long detentions before later acquittals or bail.

Post-retirement, Carpio Morales continues advocacies for good governance -- notably, the ICC communication with the late Albert del Rosario against Xi Jinping for China's environmentally destructive activities in the South China Sea -- demonstrating 'indefatigable stamina.'
stances.rhetorical_move: post-retirement continuation framing as tribute extension

notable_anecdotes: The CA pointedly noted (in language CJ approves) that the OMB 'merely made a general statement' in finding Chiong and Montalbo guilty, ruling that '[the] reassignment and designation of the MIAA employees ... were exercised with clear intent to violate the law' WITHOUT adequate factual bases -- a public administrative-law lesson on the substantial-evidence standard.

Carpio Morales's appointment as OMB was announced 'to her utter surprise' by President Aquino during his July 25, 2011 SONA -- a month after her June 19, 2011 retirement from the SC, dramatizing the unsolicited public-service recall.
Historical-first detail: she is 'the first woman to administer the oath of office of a president (Aquino) and a vice president (Jejomar Binay), a year earlier on June 30, 2010.'

Targets-of-prosecution roll-call: GMA (who herself had named Carpio Morales associate justice), Binay, Enrile, Bong Revilla, Jinggoy Estrada -- nonbailable charges, detention pending trial -- emphasizing she did not spare her appointing-president's allies.

'Three Furies' Inquirer designation in 2014: Carpio Morales, then justice secretary Leila de Lima, and COA chair Grace Pulido-Tan jointly named 'Filipino of the Year' -- pairing CJ's tribute with media recognition.

Joint ICC communication with the late Albert del Rosario against Xi Jinping -- a striking late-career act, naming a head of state for environmental crimes in the South China Sea, that links A75 directly to A80's SCS theme.

Self-reference embedded in style: 'CONSISTENT WITH THE NEW SUPREME COURT STYLEBOOK, the appellate court -- in simple language -- advanced two main reasons' -- the OMB column compliments the CA for adopting the simplicity-and-clarity standard CJ celebrates in the very next week's A76.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Court of Appeals' March 21, 2024 reversal in Chiong v. Anonymous MIAA Officials (Thirteenth Division, per J Eleuterio L. Bathan) of the Office of the Ombudsman's Aug. 1, 2023 decision dismissing Manila International Airport Authority Acting General Manager Cesar M. Chiong and Acting Assistant General Manager Irene P. Montalbo for Grave Misconduct, Abuse of Authority, and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service. Praising the CA for writing 'in simple language' consistent with the new SC Stylebook, CJ summarizes its two reasons: first, the Civil Service Commission -- not the OMB -- has primary jurisdiction to determine the legality and propriety of the 285 employee reassignments, so the OMB's decision was 'struck down for prematurity and lack of factual and legal bases' absent a prior CSC ruling; second, even granting OMB's independent examination, the verdict 'lack[ed] factual basis and substantial support in evidence,' offering only 'a general statement' without adequate factual bases. He explains the OMB's plenary 'protector of the people' role under Article XI Section 5 must be exercised with respect for respondents' constitutional rights and the powers of coequal independent bodies like the CSC, mapping the appellate pathways (OMB administrative cases to the CA; criminal cases to the Sandiganbayan; direct SC route for constitutional violations or grave abuse). He then turns to 'perhaps the most celebrated OMB,' Justice Conchita Carpio Morales, whose surprise appointment by President Aquino during his July 25, 2011 SONA came a month after her June 19, 2011 SC retirement; she had earlier been the first woman to administer presidential and vice-presidential oaths (Aquino and Binay, June 30, 2010), and during her seven-year term (2011-2018) relentlessly filed nonbailable cases against GMA (who had named her associate justice), Binay, Enrile, Bong Revilla, and Jinggoy Estrada -- earning her the Inquirer's 2014 'Filipino of the Year' as one of the 'Three Furies' (with de Lima and Pulido-Tan), a UP honoris causa doctorate in law, and the 2016 Ramon Magsaysay Award ('Asia's Nobel Prize'). 'A hero to many and a heel to others' -- critics cite the 'baseless' charges later resulting in acquittals or bail -- she continues advocacies for good governance even in retirement, notably the ICC communication she filed with the late Albert del Rosario against Chinese President Xi Jinping for China's environmentally destructive activities in the South China Sea.
